1) 24 families were identified in the Netherlands who satisfy the set of criteria for familial breast cancer, and 2) these 24 families are clinically heterogeneous, with a wide variation in the age at diagnosis of breast cancer and in the proportion of symptomatic and presymptomatic breast cancer patients.

the clinical heterogeneity of heredity breast cancer.
the clinical heterogeneity of heredity breast cancer and its implications for screening protocols.
the heterogeneity of heritable breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the clinical heterogeneity of heredity breast cancer has an impact on the screening protocols.
presymptomatic surveillance in families with hereditary breast cancer may not be beneficial in terms of survival and should therefore be discouraged.
presymptomatic surveillance is beneficial to the patient, but not in all families and not for all patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the Dutch experience on hereditary breast cancer, screening is effective in reducing breast cancer related mortality.
the majority of families with hereditary breast cancer are of a late onset type.
hereditary breast cancer families are not a homogenous group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hereditary breast cancer is a heterogeneous disease with a variety of different clinical manifestations.
the clinical heterogeneity of heredity breast cancer is reflected in the clinical course and the screening results.
